findings.reason: The protected Python solution traverses the linked list starting at head. When current.next is negative, it detaches current.next and prepends it to head (updating head), while keeping current on non-negative nodes. This sorts the linked list in linear time O(N) and O(1) auxiliary space without comparison sorting; no candidate is required.

Since nodes are given sorted by absolute value, non-negative nodes are already in non-decreasing order, while negative nodes encountered later have larger magnitudes (more negative values). Prepending each negative node to head reverses the negative nodes into correct non-decreasing signed order ahead of the non-negative chain.
Each node is inspected and relinked at most once in a single pass, using O(N) time and O(1) auxiliary space. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts a ListNode head sorted by absolute value, relinks existing nodes in-place, and returns the head of the sorted list.

The approach accurately details relative sign ordering, prepending negative nodes to head, and O(N) time / O(1) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover collecting/sorting values, insertion sort, non-negative lists, all-negative lists, equal absolute value ties, zero placement, duplicate values, and single-node lists.

App Python and native Python solutions both execute the exact same single-pass negative node prepending algorithm with SHA-256 digests 45fc7d0c04a8e93ecc14847b02396f41f18cf93d6cb4d220164b06115eec0c10 and 096e7a173fae82bf7e1fbb06c40c2467a05e3aeb695d3214d65c3c2f63e308be.
